monthly_review.summary: This month shows a marked reduction in training volume and intensity compared to last month, with lower total km, fewer runs, slower average pace, and significantly less time spent in higher HR zones — indicating a deliberate or unintentional downshift toward recovery or base-building.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 3+ time dropped from 45% of total HR distribution last month (z3+z4+z5 = 26+15+4) to just 13% this month (z3+z4+z5 = 12+1+0), signaling a substantial shift away from threshold and hard efforts.

goal_tracker.message: You need 21.1 more km across at least 6 additional sessions in the remaining 23 days to match last month’s volume — averaging ~3.5 km per session, ideally distributed as 3–4 easy Zone 1–2 runs and 2–3 moderate Zone 2–3 efforts.

insights.title: Declining efficiency despite lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.1 m/sec per bpm while average HR decreased — suggesting reduced neuromuscular coordination or form breakdown at slower paces, possibly linked to fatigue or inconsistent cadence (e.g., 133 spm on 4.6 km run vs 148 spm on 3.2 km).

insights.title: Near-total absence of Zone 4–5 work
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution shows 0% in Zone 5 and only 1% in Zone 4 — a sharp drop from 4% and 15% respectively last month — indicating loss of high-intensity stimulus critical for VO2 max maintenance and lactate buffering.

insights.title: Stride length variability correlates with pace and fatigue
insights.body: Stride length dropped from 88.65 cm at 7.77 min/km (4/29) to 66.49 cm at 10.55 min/km (5/6), while ground contact time rose from 311 ms to 351 ms — confirming inefficient mechanics during the long, slow run, likely due to accumulated fatigue or under-recovery.

insights.title: Lowest aerobic TE since April, but HR remains controlled
insights.body: Average aerobic TE this month is 2.7 (down from 3.1), yet average HR is 130 bpm — suggesting either effective recovery or insufficient stimulus; however, the 9.5 km run had only 3.0 TE despite duration, implying diminishing returns without higher intensity.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run tomorrow (HR 135–145 bpm) at consistent 8:30–8:45 min/km pace, focusing on maintaining cadence ≥142 spm using metronome cues.
recommendations.reason: Cadence dropped to 133 spm on your 4.6 km run (5/2) and 141 spm on the 9.5 km (5/6); rebuilding rhythm in Zone 2 will reinforce neuromuscular efficiency without overstressing HR.

recommendations.action: Add one 8-minute Zone 3 interval (HR 148–158 bpm) embedded in a 6 km Zone 2 run this week — e.g., after 2 km warm-up, run 4 × 2-min at Zone 3 with 90-sec walk/jog recovery, then 2 km cool-down.
recommendations.reason: Zone 3 contribution fell to 12% this month from 26% last month; reintroducing short, controlled threshold efforts will support aerobic power without excessive fatigue.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 km ‘form check’ run at 9:00 min/km on flat terrain, focusing exclusively on minimizing vertical oscillation (<7.5 cm) and keeping ground contact <310 ms — use Garmin’s real-time metrics if available.
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation ranged 7.1–8.2 cm and ground contact 301–351 ms recently; targeting lower values at slow pace builds economy and reduces injury risk.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish neuromuscular coordination through cadence consistency and controlled HR-zone transitions, while gently reintroducing threshold stimulus to prevent aerobic power decay.
suggested_sessions: 3 km form-focused easy run (target <7.5 cm VO, <310 ms GCT)
